title: Make peace between them
hook: believers are brothers, so make peace between your brothers (49:9–10)
carry: repair with fairness, so the thing can hold

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was fatabayyanu: make it clear before you act on news. Your line: verify first.

Some families have two people who don't speak. Two brothers after an inheritance. Two sisters after a wedding. Two old friends after one sentence nobody can take back. Everyone around them learns the choreography: separate invitations, careful seating, nobody saying the other's name. Years can go by like that, and it's easy to decide it isn't your business. Surah Al-Hujurat says otherwise. It makes the people standing around the quarrel responsible for ending it.

Verse nine begins with the hardest case: two groups of believers actually fighting. Make peace between them, it says; if one keeps transgressing, stand against it until it returns, then make peace with justice, and be fair. Then verse ten, in Pickthall's translation: "The believers are naught else than brothers. Therefor make peace between your brethren and observe your duty to Allah that haply ye may obtain mercy." Brothers here is ikhwah, and some commentators note it's the plural used for brothers by birth: the family word. The command, aslihu, comes from the root s-l-h, to set right, to repair. Islah is mending, the way you'd mend a torn thing so it can be used again. Peace here isn't passive. It's work, and it's assigned to bystanders. A hadith in the collections of Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi makes the point sharply. The Prophet ﷺ asked his Companions: shall I tell you of something better in rank than voluntary fasting, prayer and charity? They said yes. He said: setting things right between people, because ruining relations between people is the shaver, the thing that shaves away faith. Another hadith, in Bukhari, says that the one who makes peace between people, passing on good or saying good, is not a liar. The tradition gives the peacemaker room. And verse nine insists on justice: making peace isn't pretending nobody was wronged.

segments.voice: Bring to mind two people you know who are at odds: not a war you can't touch, but something close enough to reach. Picture each face, and think of one true, kind thing each has said or could say about the other; that's the material a peacemaker works with. If you pray, you can pray for them both.
Islah: mending, setting right, assigned by 49:10 to the people standing around a quarrel. Today's word.
Your line: repair with fairness, so the thing can hold. Peace like that takes work. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: In Muslim communities, elders, imams and family members act as go-betweens to reconcile quarrels, often citing 49:10 and the hadith that setting things right between people outranks voluntary worship.
